prefer to wait a few days to discover the expansion. For the others,

Well, this expansion seems to have a lot of pretty damn cool cards !

The Assamite starter was fun to play, even with its low number of
additional strikes (no Blurs !) and its total lack of pool gain. I was
quite surprised that Assamite can now make deadly combat at close
range too (Thin Blood+Dagon's Call, and add Disease if you feel like
it). The Giovannis stil haven't convinced me, although they now have
cool vampires. The Ravnos seem to be quite powerful now, even if the
Path of Paradox seems not to have been printed. Well, at least there's
one Ravnos who has cheaper Chimerstry cards. As for the Setites...
I'll only say that Free States Rant+Form of Corruption is... well,
deadly. I liked the concept of the two little non-unique vampires
(Aabt Kindred and Fida'i). Too bad Aabt guys don't have any obfuscate,
though.

Sensory Deprivation lets vampires vote, leaving a hostile vote deck
an unmanageable problem as long as there is one vampire capable of acting.
Reality hoses their votes, opening up the situation to friendlier vote
blocks across the table or empowering the Edge-holder. Fewer votes
means each vote counts for more, which the Ravnos and their paucity
of votes like.

The answer to that seems pretty obvious to me. It's a general rule
in all multiplayer games that you automatically increase your chances
of winning when you bring down the leader. There's lots of exceptions
to that in specific situations, of course, but it's still a good rule
of thumb in most games.

In Jyhad, the one thing that affects that thinking a lot is the predator-
prey relationships. So you always need to use judgment about what anything
you do to other players helps you or hinders you in terms of surviving your
predator and ousting your prey. But kill-the-leader is still part of this
game, too. It doesn't do to destroy your predator if it just means he gets
ousted and you get an even stronger predator in the deal. Sometimes cross-
table banishments to take out (or usually just delay) a scary grandpredator's
key minion make a lot of sense for just the reason Johan is talking about.

Actually, I think both things (that Gomi and Johan) are wrong. I think
Banishments in this game are too important to bother having even the
slightest "general principal" about. Every situation needs careful
consideration.
